title: What changes when EMC studies are read together?
scope: A bounded synthesis of selected reviewed clinical, molecular and model studies. This is not a completed review of every EMC publication. Rankings are research judgments, not treatment recommendations or calculated probabilities of success.
conclusion: The strongest experimental lead here is to separate proteasome sensitivity from the mechanism that makes a combination work. The strongest clinical question is what distinguishes exceptional multikinase-inhibitor responders. Neither has an established predictive biomarker. The immune findings currently support careful sample matching, not a universal EMC immune subtype.

sources.label: Bangerter 2023 · two EMC models
sources.location: Molecular characterization; functional characterization; Figures 4–6; Supplementary Table 1
sources.denominator: Two patient-derived models: USZ20-EMC1 (EWSR1–NR4A3) and USZ22-EMC2 (TAF15–NR4A3). One donor per fusion class.
sources.observation: Carfilzomib was active in both models. Venetoclax alone was inactive in validation; carfilzomib combinations were synergistic in USZ20 and additive in USZ22.
sources.limitation: Six-day viability assays; culture, patient history and secondary alterations differ. No normal-cell therapeutic window established. A fusion-partner effect cannot be separated from donor background.
sources.reading: Body, references, all six figures and both supplementary tables reviewed; original response matrices unavailable in this review.

sources.label: Iwata 2025 · NCC-EMC1-C1
sources.location: Supplementary Table 3, rows 31/41/217; Supplementary Table 4, row 6
sources.denominator: One additional patient-derived EMC model; one drug-screen report.
sources.observation: Screen mean viability: bortezomib 13.6%, carfilzomib 23.6%, venetoclax 79.5%. The separate concentration-response table reports bortezomib IC50 135 nM.
sources.limitation: Screen concentration, exposure duration and replicate count unresolved because main methods remain inaccessible. These values cannot be pooled with the Zurich assays; the screen does not test the combination.
sources.reading: Primary abstract and supplementary Tables 1, 3 and 4 reviewed; main methods/figures incomplete.

sources.label: O'Sullivan Coyne 2022 · cabozantinib trial
sources.location: Antitumor activity; Figure 2; Supplementary Figure S1
sources.denominator: Three EMC patients enrolled; 54 of 55 sarcoma patients were evaluable overall. One EMC patient had a confirmed partial response.
sources.observation: The EMC responder first responded after ten cycles and remained on treatment through 99 cycles. Supplement S1 indicates no prior VEGF-targeting therapy.
sources.limitation: No responder-specific tumor genotype or activated-MET result reported. Treatment duration is not response duration. Overall trial efficacy thresholds were not met.
sources.reading: Body, references, three tables, three figures and three supplementary figures reviewed.

sources.label: He 2022 · changes across samples
sources.denominator: One NR4A3-rearranged EMC patient; four samples across sites and treatment time points.
sources.observation: EGFR/MET copy gains and FBXW7 variants differed across samples. The patient progressed on doxorubicin/ifosfamide; proposed targeted drugs were not administered.
sources.limitation: No functional validation, no primary-tumor sequencing and prior-chemotherapy confounding. Table 1 mislabels splice/stop notation as missense; copy gain is not demonstrated pathway dependence.
sources.reading: Body, references, main table and five figures reviewed; supplementary DOCX text read; workbook inventory only.

sources.label: Zou 2023 · longitudinal genomes
sources.denominator: One patient; primary, lung and pelvic tumor samples plus blood.
sources.observation: The defining fusion persisted across tumors while additional variants differed. DMBT1 copy loss also appeared in blood.
sources.limitation: Coverage confounds variant-count comparisons. No expression or drug-response validation; DMBT1 loss is not established as tumor-specific.
sources.reading: Body, references, two tables and eight figures reviewed; targeted supplementary workbook checks only.

sources.label: Stacchiotti 2012 · withdrawal and retreatment
sources.denominator: Two EWSR1-rearranged EMC patients; possible overlap with the subsequent ten-patient series.
sources.observation: Sunitinib activity included a withdrawal/progression/reintroduction pattern in one patient.
sources.limitation: Uncontrolled cases; infection affected the interruption. Retreatment supports drug association, not the identity of the inhibited target. Do not add these patients to the later series without linkage.

sources.label: Stacchiotti 2019 · pazopanib
sources.denominator: 26 enrolled; 23 modified intention-to-treat; 22 response-evaluable; four partial responses.
sources.observation: Objective activity with another multikinase/anti-angiogenic agent provides a competing explanation for cabozantinib benefit.
sources.limitation: Uncontrolled trial; different population and exposure. Primary full text and the linked correction require completion; no indirect drug comparison is justified.
sources.reading: Abstract reviewed; full article and correction contents incomplete.

sources.label: NCT05836571 · existing biomarker study
sources.location: Protocol description, secondary/exploratory objectives; registry API checked 2026-09-17
sources.denominator: Mixed-sarcoma randomized protocol that includes EMC; no posted results at this check.
sources.observation: Compares ipilimumab/nivolumab with or without cabozantinib; plans CD8, CD3/CD68, ctDNA and total/activated MET measurements.
sources.limitation: Active, not recruiting at this check. A planned measurement is not a result. The design does not isolate cabozantinib's MET effect from its other actions.
sources.reading: Registry status, design, eligibility and stated objectives checked; not a completed outcome study.

sources.label: Ogata 2022 · pleural immune environment
sources.denominator: One pleural-metastatic EMC patient with a reported NR4A3/EWSR1 fusion.
sources.observation: Macrophage-rich tissue, sparse CD8 cells, absent FOXP3 staining, negative PD-L1 and TGF-beta1/VEGF staining; TMB 4 mutations/Mb.
sources.limitation: One site/time point. Staining does not demonstrate cytokine secretion, suppressive function or drug dependence. TGF-beta/VEGF combinations were already proposed by the authors.
sources.reading: Body, references, four figures and graphical abstract reviewed.

sources.label: PeerJ 2026 · expression and immune staining
sources.location: Methods; Figure 4; Supplementary Figures S3–S6; expression workbook
sources.denominator: 12 patients in expression model; five reported model events; immune imaging in two selected specimens with multiple regions.
sources.observation: The selected high-risk specimen showed FOXP3-positive cells; the selected low-risk specimen did not. PXN/TYMS/H1FX formed an exploratory prognostic score.
sources.limitation: Regions are not independent patients. Severe model overfitting, source-label conflicts and incomplete molecular confirmation limit inference. No drug response linked to the expression workbook.
sources.reading: Body, references, main/supplement figures reviewed; workbook audited; supplementary Word layout pending.

sources.label: Papadopoulos 2018 · anti-Hu encephalitis
sources.location: Case report; supplementary antibody and clinical data
sources.denominator: One EMC patient treated with REGN2810/cemiplimab.
sources.observation: Tumor shrinkage below the partial-response threshold co-occurred with fatal encephalitis; anti-Hu antibodies were present before treatment.
sources.limitation: An immune response is not equivalent to net clinical benefit. This case cannot estimate toxicity frequency or establish a universal exclusion rule.
sources.reading: Body, figures and two supplements reviewed.

sources.label: Long-term observation 2020
sources.denominator: Three selected EMC patients followed without systemic therapy for 50, 70 and 126 months.
sources.observation: Prolonged courses can occur without systemic therapy.
sources.limitation: Selected cases, not a matched untreated control; some patients had local treatments or progression. Follow-up duration is not progression-free survival.

sources.label: Jennings 2021 · KIT-selected imatinib
sources.denominator: One NR4A3-rearranged EMC with a somatic KIT W557G variant.
sources.observation: Approximately three years of stable disease on imatinib were reported.
sources.limitation: No EMC functional test or controlled counterfactual. Stable disease alone cannot establish the magnitude of drug benefit.

sources.label: Kim 2007 · old fusion nomenclature
sources.location: Abstract; interaction mapping and reporter experiments
sources.denominator: Engineered non-EMC cellular/biochemical systems, not patient-derived EMC drug testing.
sources.observation: GAPDH interacted with hTAFII68–TEC (TAF15–NR4A3) and enhanced transcriptional reporter activity.
sources.limitation: The interaction is prior art. It does not establish glycolytic dependence, a druggable interface or therapeutic selectivity.
sources.reading: Abstract and substantial indexed primary text reviewed; full figure-level verification outstanding.

sources.label: 2026 retraction of the myeloma SGK1 paper
sources.denominator: A non-EMC mechanistic supporting paper, not an EMC clinical study.
sources.observation: The paper previously used to support the SGK1/proteasome-resistance bridge was retracted.
sources.limitation: That bridge is withdrawn. Independent EMC drug-screen findings remain separate evidence and do not repair the retracted mechanism.
sources.reading: Retraction status checked and public correction recorded in the literature report.

hypotheses.title: Separate proteasome sensitivity from combination sensitization
hypotheses.status: Priority for mechanistic testing; not a demonstrated treatment
hypotheses.inference: Across two publications, three donor models support proteasome-inhibitor activity more consistently than venetoclax monotherapy. A plausible explanation is that proteasome stress creates a conditional vulnerability to an apoptosis-targeting partner. That mechanism has not been measured in these EMC experiments.
hypotheses.against: Additivity in USZ22 weakens a universal-synergy claim. Generic toxicity, schedule effects, or different cell-growth rates could explain the pattern. One donor per fusion class cannot identify a fusion-specific mechanism.
hypotheses.available_test: Completed here: a reproducible extraction of the three named drugs from the independent screen, retaining SD, original rows and missing methods. This checks directional consistency only; it does not estimate a combined effect.
hypotheses.missing_test: Matched dose/time response matrices in all models, with early target engagement, apoptosis/mitochondrial-priming measurements, selective perturbation/rescue and nonmalignant controls. These require laboratory work or unreleased data.
hypotheses.falsifier: If combination benefit disappears after matching single-agent effect, or does not track induced apoptotic susceptibility, the sensitization interpretation weakens. Equal killing of relevant normal cells would defeat the proposed selectivity.
hypotheses.novelty: The drugs and combinations were already proposed in 2023. The added synthesis is to prioritize conditional partner dependence over baseline BCL-2 expression. A targeted search found no independent EMC validation of this mechanism; that is not proof of novelty.
hypotheses.decision: First experimental question to resolve, not a reason to prescribe the combination. Do not use the withdrawn SGK1 bridge as its mechanism.

hypotheses.title: Distinguish tumor MET activity from vascular and immune effects
hypotheses.status: Clinically relevant; existing prospective work; outcome linkage missing
hypotheses.inference: An exceptional cabozantinib response, MET gain in a different patient's evolving tumor, and responses to other multikinase agents generate competing explanations. The key question is whether activated tumor MET predicts benefit beyond vascular effects, rather than whether a MET-related observation exists somewhere in EMC.
hypotheses.against: The responder's MET status is unknown; copy gain alone is not activation. Benefit from other drugs is compatible with anti-angiogenesis. Cabozantinib targets several kinases, and the current combination trial cannot causally isolate one target.
hypotheses.available_test: Completed here: check the existing trial's prespecified MET/immune measurements and posted-result status. No public patient-level EMC table currently joins activated MET, drug exposure and response in the sources reviewed.
hypotheses.missing_test: Link pretreatment and on-treatment EMC specimens to lesion-level response, prior VEGF therapy, fusion and secondary alterations. Compare tumor-cell MET perturbation with endothelial effects; a marker-outcome association alone would remain insufficient for causality.
hypotheses.falsifier: Consistent response without tumor MET activation would weaken MET as a selection marker. Compartment-specific perturbation/rescue experiments, controlling baseline viability and drug exposure, could distinguish tumor-MET dependence from vascular-pathway dependence.
hypotheses.novelty: MET-directed therapy was proposed in the 2022 genetic case. NCT05836571 already prespecifies activated-MET and immune analyses. This is a sharper interpretation plan for existing work, not a newly discovered target.
hypotheses.decision: Prioritize outcome-linked biomarker evidence. Do not infer benefit after pazopanib failure from a cabozantinib responder who had no prior VEGF-targeting treatment.

hypotheses.title: Test whether immune differences reflect sampling context
hypotheses.inference: Macrophage-rich, FOXP3-negative pleural disease and a FOXP3-positive selected high-risk specimen need not represent contradictory universal tumor classes. Site, treatment history, assay and spatial sampling could account for the difference. Immune-state claims should therefore be tied to specimen context before being used to select combinations.
hypotheses.against: The image evidence spans very few patients, uses different assays and includes imperfect diagnostic confirmation. Low TMB or negative PD-L1 does not by itself prove resistance. Shrinkage and immune activation do not establish a favorable benefit-risk balance.
hypotheses.available_test: The public expression workbook has 12 samples but no linked treatment-response outcomes. Region-level staining comparisons cannot supply independent patient replication. The matrix records this lack of testable outcome linkage rather than fitting a predictive model.
hypotheses.missing_test: Harmonized patient-level specimen metadata and common staining/analysis methods; preferably matched sites or time points. Test whether differences survive adjustment for purity, site and prior treatment before defining a subgroup.
hypotheses.falsifier: If differences disappear with a shared assay and matched sampling, a stable biological immune-subtype interpretation fails. If they persist within matched conditions, specimen context alone is insufficient.
hypotheses.novelty: Immune/vascular combinations and prospective immune measurements already exist. The contribution here is an explicit competing-explanation and sampling plan, not a new immune drug combination.
hypotheses.decision: Do not turn these small, heterogeneous observations into an EMC-wide immune classification or a response score.

hypotheses.title: Use pretreatment growth and retreatment to judge apparent benefit
hypotheses.status: Evidence-selection rule that changes which treatment leads deserve attention
hypotheses.inference: Long untreated courses make prolonged stable disease difficult to interpret. Pairing those observations with drug withdrawal/reintroduction and confirmed shrinkage suggests prioritizing within-patient changes in growth rate over duration on treatment alone.
hypotheses.against: Observation cohorts are selected and cannot serve as trial controls. Withdrawal episodes may be confounded by infection or local intervention. Neither a single partial response nor retreatment establishes general efficacy.
hypotheses.available_test: A source-level outcome audit is possible now: retain pretreatment trajectory, RECIST response, interruption/restart, local procedures and censoring separately. Do not pool these reports into a synthetic response rate.
hypotheses.missing_test: Original serial scans or lesion measurements and dates. Compare each patient's pretreatment and on-treatment slopes under a prespecified approach, with sensitivity checks for measurement error and treatment-triggered selection.
hypotheses.falsifier: If growth remains unchanged across treatment initiation and interruptions, attribution of stable disease to the drug weakens. Reproducible slope changes strengthen association but still need replication.
hypotheses.novelty: EMC's indolence and retreatment observations are known. This is a cross-report adjudication rule, not a novel biological mechanism.
hypotheses.decision: Rank the cabozantinib partial response and informative retreatment histories above uncontextualized stable-disease anecdotes, without equating this research priority with a treatment ranking.

hypotheses.title: Revisit a fusion-cofactor interaction in a modern EMC model
hypotheses.inference: The older GAPDH–TAF15/TEC interaction can now be examined in a molecularly confirmed TAF15–NR4A3 donor model. This creates a way to distinguish a fusion-associated transcriptional role from generic glycolysis, which a conventional metabolic-inhibitor screen would not resolve.
hypotheses.against: The original experiments used engineered non-EMC systems. The relevant interaction may not be necessary in native tumors, and selectively perturbing it without disturbing essential GAPDH functions may be infeasible.
hypotheses.available_test: Map old fusion names and reported interaction domains to the actual USZ22 fusion junction before proposing a perturbation. The original paper's complete figures and sequence-level compatibility still need review; no binding calculation is treated as validation.
hypotheses.missing_test: Confirm endogenous interaction, then distinguish interface disruption from catalytic inhibition using matched controls and rescue. Compare with EWSR1-fusion and nonmalignant models. This cannot be established computationally from expression correlations.
hypotheses.falsifier: No endogenous interaction, incompatible fusion architecture, or a phenotype explained entirely by loss of glycolysis would undermine the selective cofactor route.
hypotheses.novelty: The interaction is established prior art; the later model provides a testing opportunity. No claim that this particular native-model experiment has never been attempted.
hypotheses.decision: A lower-priority mechanistic route after sequence and source verification; not a rationale for nonspecific GAPDH inhibition.

rejected_shortcuts.title: SGK1 explains proteasome resistance in EMC
rejected_shortcuts.reason: Withdrawn: a key supporting myeloma paper was retracted. Independent drug activity cannot validate that mechanism.

rejected_shortcuts.title: A prognostic RNA signature selects TYMS-directed treatment
rejected_shortcuts.reason: Not established: outcome association, severe overfitting and unlinked drug-response data do not demonstrate dependency or treatment benefit.

rejected_shortcuts.title: One fusion partner predicts combination synergy
rejected_shortcuts.reason: Not identifiable from one donor per fusion class; patient background, secondary alterations and culture history are confounded.

novelty_search.method: Targeted web searches plus discussion/reference checks in the linked primary sources. Limited scope; no claim of exhaustive novelty clearance.
